title: HTML6 Template Engine
description: A lightweight, component-based server-side template engine for building fast, dynamic HTML from plain JavaScript. It's the engine powering this site's own rendering.
longDescription: HTML6 is a server-side template engine that compiles plain HTML into fast, reusable render functions. The motivation was for someone who only knows HTML and CSS to be able to write conditionals, loops, and components without ever touching JavaScript or a framework like React.
challenge: The goal was for HTML6 to be the fastest template engine out there, not just a workable one. The catch: tags like if/elsif/else need to see their siblings to resolve correctly, and the obvious way to handle that means walking the parsed tree more than once, exactly the kind of overhead a fastest-in-class claim can't afford.
solution:
HTML6 compiles by walking the parsed tree exactly once, bottom-up, dispatching each node only after its children are done. The technique that makes that possible is masking and unmasking.

Tags that need sibling context, like an if/elsif/else chain or a map loop, get masked instead of resolved inline: swapped for a placeholder key in a lookup table so the walk never has to backtrack. Once that single pass finishes, unmasking swaps every placeholder back to its real content, and the result is wrapped into a native JavaScript render function.
features: Real .html files, no build step required
Conditions and expressions are real JavaScript
Components with slots and isolated props
Compiles once, renders every request from that function
Missing a variable fails loud, never silent

title: uLearn
description: A production AI language-learning platform I designed, built, and operate solo — real-time voice tutoring, adaptive flashcards, and per-language grammar handling across four languages, running on six independent Go microservices.
longDescription:
uLearn is a language-learning platform for German, English, Russian, and French, built around one idea: reading, vocabulary review, and AI tutoring should reinforce each other instead of living in separate apps.

It runs as six independent Go services — an LLM-backed content service, speech-to-text, text-to-speech, a text generator, email, and the core API — plus a web frontend, all deployed on AWS. **I designed, built, and still operate every part of it solo**, from the AWS infrastructure to the subscription billing.
challenge:
The hard part wasn't wiring up an LLM — it was that four languages don't share a grammar. German needs case and declension handling, Russian needs its own conjugation and declension logic, French verb tables don't map onto either. A single generic "ask the model" approach falls apart the moment a learner needs an accurate grammatical breakdown, not just a plausible-sounding one.

The second challenge was latency: a voice conversation with an AI tutor has to feel real-time, which meant the speech-to-text, LLM, and text-to-speech legs of that pipeline all needed to be fast and independently scalable — not one monolith blocking on the slowest step.
solution:
Each language got its own grammar-handling code — conjugation and declension logic per language, not one shared black box — living inside a dedicated content service that also generates flashcards and word lookups. That service calls an LLM for the generation itself, but the surrounding logic (what's asked, how it's structured, how it's validated) is deterministic, not the model improvising grammar.

Splitting speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and the LLM content service into independent Go services let each one scale and fail on its own — a slow TTS call doesn't block a flashcard being generated elsewhere. The whole thing runs on AWS (ECS, EC2, DynamoDB), provisioned with Pulumi, with the web frontend served through HTML6 — the same template engine I built at Eldøy Projects, now running my own product in production.
features: Real-time voice conversations with an AI tutor, with contextual corrections
Automatic flashcard generation from any word or phrase while reading
Interactive YouTube transcripts with clickable word lookup
Per-language grammar handling — German declension, Russian conjugation, French verb tables
Free, Pro, and Premium subscription tiers
